Crop the image into a perfectly square frame instead

questions.stem: On Rule of thirds: a designer reviewing a craft brewery's label notices that a photograph places the main subject dead center and feels static. Which compositional change typically adds more tension?

options.text: Center the subject even more precisely in the frame
options.misconception: reinforces the very static composition being criticized

options.text: Crop the image into a perfectly square frame instead
options.misconception: changes the frame shape rather than the subject placement

options.text: Reduce the overall resolution of the image being used
options.misconception: substitutes a technical property for a compositional choice

options.text: Move the subject onto one of the thirds intersections

questions.explanation: The rule of thirds divides the frame into a three-by-three grid and suggests placing key elements along those lines or intersections. Off-center placement creates more visual tension and interest than a rigid centering of the subject.
questions.hint: Where are the points of interest in a three-by-three frame?

options.text: A strict rule that every column must be equal in width
options.misconception: confuses a particular ratio with simple equality of parts

options.text: The whole relates to the larger part as the larger relates to the smaller
A measure of the overall ink density of a layout
options.misconception: mistakes tonal balance for a relationship of proportions

options.text: A grid that is required to have exactly three columns
options.misconception: reduces a proportion to a mere count of columns

questions.explanation: The golden ratio is a proportion in which the whole divided by the larger part equals the larger part divided by the smaller. Designers use such ratios to divide space in a way that many find naturally harmonious, without making the parts equal.

questions.learningObjective: evaluate golden ratio proportion in a design critique
questions.stem: On Golden ratio proportion: a designer reviewing a government services form notices that a designer wants a pleasing ratio between two column widths. Which idea describes this system of proportion?

options.text: The whole relates to the larger part as the larger relates to the smaller
A strict rule that every column must be equal in width
options.misconception: confuses a particular ratio with simple equality of parts

options.text: A measure of the overall ink density of a layout
options.misconception: mistakes tonal balance for a relationship of proportions

options.text: A grid that is required to have exactly three columns
options.misconception: reduces a proportion to a mere count of columns

questions.explanation: The golden ratio is a proportion in which the whole divided by the larger part equals the larger part divided by the smaller. Designers use such ratios to divide space in a way that many find naturally harmonious, without making the parts equal.
questions.hint: Is this a relationship between parts or a fixed number of columns?
